title: Guide
intro: A tool for building Genshin Impact combat rotations (who uses what, and when) along a timeline, and checking Skill/Burst cooldowns and buff overlaps. Rotations are saved only in this browser.

items.1: Open Team Setup and choose the 4 party members (character, constellation, weapon, artifacts).
items.2: Under "Add stint" in the middle of the screen, press a character's button to line up stints (one on-field turn of that character). The same character can appear any number of times.
items.3: Inside each stint, press buttons such as +N +C +tE +hE +Q +D +J +Wait to add actions.
items.4: Check the timeline, Skill/Burst cooldowns, effect durations, buff overlaps and cooldown conflicts on the Gantt chart below.
items.5: For precise numbers, press Run gcsim (the real simulator measures action times, cooldowns, durations and triggered buffs, and applies them).
items.6: When you are happy with it, use Save as (saved rotation). Copy notation creates a one-line notation you can post on social media.

items.1: Top row: choose a saved rotation, Save, Save as / play and reset (cycle, time, speed 0.5x–2x) / cooldown status (No cooldown conflicts / Cooldown conflicts / Cooldown warnings) / Hide (show or hide the button row below).
items.2: Button row: Guide / Team Setup, Rotations, Database / Run gcsim, Copy gcsim config, Back to app calculation / Copy notation (and the current notation, with Short/Names switch).
items.3: Build area (list of stints): edit the order and the actions here. The chips of "Quick reorder" above change the stint order at a glance.
items.4: Gantt chart: the horizontal axis is time (seconds). From the top: stint flow, number of overlapping buffs (Synergy), and one row per character (actions, cooldowns, effects, triggered buffs). Zoom with the slider at the top right.

items.1: Where actions are added: when one action is selected with a click, the add buttons insert before it (in the same stint). With nothing selected, or another stint selected, actions are added at the end. Click the stint background to clear the selection.
items.2: Reordering: drag and drop actions (within the same stint; the switch action stays first). Stints can be moved with the card's drag handle, "Up/Down", dragging the quick reorder chips, or dragging on the Gantt chart. After reordering, later times reconnect automatically (serial snapping).
items.3: Action time: change each action's time with ▲▼ (0.05 s, 0.1 s) or by typing a number. For hold skills (hE), you can also set how long to hold. Changed values are marked, and "Back to app calculation" restores them all.
items.4: Delete: the ✕ on an action. For a stint, the delete button on the right of the card (or the × on its quick reorder chip).
items.5: Add memo: you can leave a memo on each stint.

items.1: Ctrl+click actions (Cmd+click on Mac) to select adjacent ones → "Group N". With only one selected, "Repeat 1".
items.2: Set the group's count (▲▼ or a number) and the actions inside are calculated as done that many times in a row. The default is 1.
items.3: The notation becomes 3C (one action 3 times) or 2[N1C] (N1 and C twice).
items.4: Pressing Ungroup lays the actions out as normal actions with the current count (with a count of 3, three repetitions remain).
items.5: Actions inside a group can only be reordered within the group. The whole group can also be moved.

items.1: Cooldown bars (Skill CD, Burst CD): the wait until the action can be used again. Actions with a red mark have a cooldown conflict (used before the cooldown ended).
items.2: Effect bars (shields, fields, transformations, etc.): while the action's effect lasts.
items.3: Dashed-border bars (triggered buffs): effects of passive talents, weapons, artifacts and constellations, colored by type. Carried means the effect continues from the previous cycle.
items.4: Amber border / cooldown warning: triggered buffs placed during their cooldown, special skills outside their window, plunging attacks without their prerequisites, etc. Hover over the bar to see the reason.
items.5: Loop point: the start of the range repeated from the 2nd cycle on. Drag to move it. Playback lets you check the 1st and 2nd cycles.
items.6: Hover over a bar to see its name, timing and description.

items.1: "Run gcsim" runs the current team and rotation in gcsim (the simulator, running inside your browser) and applies the results at once. Nothing is sent to a server.
items.2: Applied values: action times, Skill/Burst cooldowns, effect durations, and positions and lengths of triggered buffs. If there are cooldown conflicts, it does not run (fix them first).
items.3: To discard applied values and return to the app's calculation (master frames and cooldowns), use "Back to app calculation".
items.4: "Copy gcsim config" gives you the gcsim config (to run it in gcsim elsewhere; conversion warnings are shown too).
items.5: Characters and effects gcsim does not support are marked "Not simulated" and keep the app's calculation.

items.1: Your edits are saved automatically in this browser (nothing is sent to a server). They are lost if you clear the browser data.
items.2: Rotations: save, load and delete named rotations (slots). A single rotation can also be exported to or imported from a JSON file.
items.3: Back up all data (Rotations → JSON backup & share): bundles all saved rotations, the current rotation, settings and the data you created into one file. Use it when moving to another browser or device, or before clearing data.
items.4: Database: sync, edit and add character, weapon and artifact data.

notation.title: Notation (sharing as text)

items.1: "Copy notation" copies the rotation as a one-line string. Example: {{example}}
items.2: You can switch between Short (E, Q, N1, C, etc., written compactly) and Names.
items.3: The part enclosed in {{braces}} is the range repeated from the 2nd cycle on (after the loop point).
items.4: Consecutive Normal Attacks are written N3 (3 times), groups 3C or 2[N1C], and holds hE@2.0s.

notation.example: {Furina E > Citlali E > Furina Q > Xiangling EQ}
